findings.claim: Both correction commits carry `Co-Authored-By: gpt-6-astra <noreply@openai.com>` in addition to `Co-Authored-By: Grok 4.6 <noreply@x.ai>` and `Reviewed-by: gpt-6-astra <noreply@openai.com>`. The supplied adjudicate record 20260908T082619Z-adjudicate-codex-f8dfc8 declares role 'read' with changed_paths [] and residual_paths [], so gpt-6-astra wrote no file here; AGENTS.md states 'Work you did not do gets no trailer with your name'. Read the other way — the ruling did supply the three statements verbatim — the same actor is then both co-author and approver of one artifact, and it is already Co-Authored-By on the implementation these tests exercise (ded2987 'feat(harness): isolate agy configuration under HOME'), against 'Whoever writes an implementation neither writes nor approves its tests.' The immediate precedent for this exact shape, adjudicated grok test corrections 2e45832 and 0314068, carries only `Co-Authored-By: Grok 4.6` plus `Reviewed-by: gpt-6-astra`; the added co-author trailer is an unexplained deviation. The record, not the practice, is the defect: the file edits were produced by the tests dispatch 20260908T082927Z-tests-grok-851ac6 (role 'write', changed_paths exactly the two test files). Smallest correction is a follow-up provenance note dropping the gpt-6-astra co-author trailer and keeping Reviewed-by, matching the precedent; no code change is implied and nothing about the three corrections is affected.
